name: MLPerf Tiny
description: Advancements in ultra-low-power tiny machine learning (TinyML) systems promise to unlock an entirely new class of smart applications. However, continued progress is limited by the lack of a widely accepted and easily reproducible benchmark for these systems. To meet this need, we present MLPerf Tiny, the first industry-standard benchmark suite for ultra-low-power tiny machine learning systems. The benchmark suite is the collaborative effort of more than 50 organizations from industry and academia and reflects the needs of the community. MLPerf Tiny measures the accuracy, latency, and energy of machine learning inference to properly evaluate the tradeoffs between systems. Additionally, MLPerf Tiny implements a modular design that enables benchmark submitters to show the benefits of their product, regardless of where it falls on the ML deployment stack, in a fair and reproducible manner. The suite features four benchmarks: keyword spotting, visual wake words, image classification, and anomaly detection.
evaluation_method: Task accuracy for classification tasks, plus system-level latency and energy-per-inference measurements (power/energy and throughput/latency) for hardware evaluation
general_score_metric: Per-task accuracy combined with hardware metrics (latency, energy per inference); submissions report both accuracy and system metrics.
typical_sota_score: varies by task (commonly high for KWS/VWW >85% but task-dependent)
reputation: Industry-standard TinyML benchmark suite (part of the MLPerf family) with broad industry and academic adoption for low-power inference evaluation.
notes: Non-LLM, system-level benchmark — results depend strongly on hardware and measurement methodology; reproducibility requires careful calibration; tasks/datasets are small and specialized, so applicability to large-scale generalization is limited.
